drivingQuestion: Why does Hannah's prayer say אמתך three times?
outcomeNote: Aggadic exposition of the threefold אמתך; a variant wording is recorded, nothing is contested.

segments.en: In the oath/prayer uttered by Hannah, she refers to herself as “Your servant” [amatekha] three times: «“The affliction of Your maidservant…»and «not forget Your maidservant and will give Your maidservant”» (I Samuel 1:11).

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: שָׁלֹשׁ אֲמָתוֹת הַלָּלוּ לָמָּה? — אָמְרָה חַנָּה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, שְׁלֹשָׁה בִּדְקֵי מִיתָה בָּרָאתָ בָּאִשָּׁה, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: שְׁלֹשָׁה דִּבְקֵי מִיתָה. וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: נִדָּה, וְחַלָּה וְהַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר. כְּלוּם עָבַרְתִּי עַל אַחַת מֵהֶן?! —
segments.en: «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said: Why» are «these three maidservants [amatot]» cited in the verse? They are cited to teach that «Hannah said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the Universe, You have created three crucibles» potentially leading to «death in a woman,» where she is particularly vulnerable. Alternatively, «some say:» Master of the Universe, You have created «three accelerants of death» in a woman. «They are» mitzvot that, as a rule, pertain to women: Observing the halakhot of «a menstruating woman,» separating «ḥalla» from dough, «and lighting» Shabbat «candles. Have I ever violated one of them?» Hannah attests to her status as God’s maidservant [ama]. The reference to these three mitzvot is drawn from the etymological similarity between amatekha, your maidservant, and mita, death.

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: שלש אמתות הללו למה
moves.summary: R' Yosei b. R' Ḥanina asks why 'Your maidservant' appears three times.
moves.about: why Hannah says 'Your maidservant' three times: she attests she never violated the three women's mitzvot

moves.cueHe: אמרה חנה לפני הקדוש ברוך הוא
moves.summary: Hannah told God: You created three death-crucibles in a woman — nidda, ḥalla, candle-lighting — have I violated any?
moves.about: Hannah's protest that she never violated nidda, ḥalla or candle-lighting, the three death-crucibles created in a woman

moves.summary: Variant wording of the same tradition: 'three accelerants of death'.
moves.about: whether the phrase is 'three crucibles of death' (בדקי) or 'three accelerants of death' (דבקי)
